project: OpsPilot AI — Enterprise AI Operations, Workflow & Risk Automation Platform

criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: Static Command Center at the repo root; all nine tabs read .colaberry/ at runtime. Run the checks with: node --test "tests/*.test.mjs"

criteria.text: Given multiple agents are available, when I initiate a process operation, then the system orchestrates the agents to complete the operation.
Given an agent fails during orchestration, when the system detects the failure, then it reallocates tasks to other agents.
Trust: The system logs all orchestration activities for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Orchestration core with reallocation and a hash-chained audit log; demo: node src/demo/run.js. Agents in the demo are stand-ins. REQ-001 is NOT met yet: no real Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace connector exists (needs credentials); only the connector interface is built.

criteria.text: Given a set of process data, when the analysis is initiated, then the system should provide a detailed report of inefficiencies.
Given an incomplete data set, when the analysis is attempted, then the system should notify the user of missing data.
Trust: The system logs all analysis activities with timestamps and user IDs for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Process analysis from an event log: bottlenecks, duplicated work, automation candidates, as a detailed report; incomplete data returns a missing-data notice instead; analysts and operations managers only; every step audited with user id and timestamp. Demo: node src/demo/analyse.js (synthetic data). Input is a JSON event log until a real connector exists (REQ-001).

criteria.text: Given AI systems are registered, When a risk assessment is performed, Then risks are identified and categorized.
Given AI systems are registered, When a risk assessment is performed, Then it suggests mitigation actions.
Trust: Risk assessment results are logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Risk assessment of registered AI systems with a rule-based, pluggable risk model: each system gets risks in six categories (privacy, fairness, human oversight, transparency, security, accountability) with severity, reason and suggested mitigations, plus an overall rating. Incomplete systems are reported unassessed while the rest are assessed; risk model errors mark a system failed and the run is not saved; a time limit interrupts hung models. Compliance officer, security officer and operations manager only. Every step and every system result is in the hash-chained audit log. Idempotent by assessmentId. Demo: node src/demo/riskAssessment.js (synthetic systems). Systems are supplied as JSON until the STORY-004 inventory exists.

criteria.text: Given AI systems are registered, When I view the inventory, Then it lists all systems with details.
Given AI systems are registered, When I update a system's status, Then the inventory reflects the change.
Trust: Inventory changes are logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: AI system inventory in PostgreSQL (system, department, purpose, risk, owner, status, version): view lists every system with details; status changes are reflected immediately with a new version; risk is filled from completed STORY-003 assessments. IT manager registers and updates; compliance officer, security officer and operations manager view. Every view and change is in the hash-chained audit log, written inside the database transaction. Out-of-date updates and reused ids are refused; repeats change nothing. Tests and demo run on PGlite (PostgreSQL in Node); a real server is used via DATABASE_URL with connect/query timeouts and capped retries. Demo: node src/demo/inventory.js (synthetic systems).

criteria.text: Given a workflow is automated, When a high-risk action is detected, Then it requires human approval.
Given a workflow is automated, When a low-risk action is detected, Then it executes automatically.
Trust: All automated actions are logged with risk levels.

stories.notes: Workflow automation with human oversight: each action is classified by named rules (action type, the AI system's live inventory risk, taking a system out of use, payment limit, irreversibility; an author label can raise but never lower it; unknown means high). Low-risk actions run automatically; high-risk ones wait for a process manager who did not start the workflow; after 4 h the approval escalates to operations managers and compliance officers with a reminder, and at 24 h it expires as rejected. Failed actions stop the workflow and can be resumed; every action runs once by idempotency key with timeouts and capped retries. Runs live in PostgreSQL; every action is audited with its risk level. Notify, ticket and payment are stand-ins; the inventory status change is real. Demo: node src/demo/automation.js (synthetic data).

criteria.text: Given process analysis data is available, when I access the dashboard, then I see the analysis results and automation opportunities.
Given no data is available, when I access the dashboard, then I see a message indicating no data is present.

stories.notes: Process analysis dashboard: a local web server (127.0.0.1) showing saved STORY-002 reports — latest results and automation opportunities, every analysis, full reports; a no-data message; 401/403 for unauthorised access, 503 when data cannot be read, 500 on a rendering error; every request audited with user id and timestamp before anything is shown. Demo: node src/demo/dashboard.js (synthetic data; demo sign-in, not real authentication).
